This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.
This scales the denoising threshold for very low frequencies ( very coarse detail). 0 is none, 1 is the estimated threshold.

description.plain_text: Denoise: Uses spatial or temporal filtering to remove noise or grain without losing image quality. Motion Input: An optional input for attaching pre-calculated motion vectors, such as those created by VectorGenerator. Denoise can generate motion vectors internally, but connecting this input may produce significantly faster results. Temporal Processing: When enabled, uses frames on both sides of the current frame to perform temporal frame blending, which may produce a better denoise result. The number of frames used on either side of the current frame is determined by the Temporal Frame Offset control. When disabled, uses only the current frame to produce the denoise result. Frame Blending: Sets the variance allowed between regions in blended frames. Higher values attempt to blend more regions, but can lose image detail. This control is only available when Temporal Processing is enabled. Temporal Frame Offset: Sets the number of frames, on either side of the current frame, used to calculate the denoise effect.This control is only available when Temporal Processing is enabled. Lift Blacks: When enabled, blacks in the image are lifted toward white. This can be particularly useful if your image contains a lot of sub-blacks, areas of black with a value less than 0. Preserve Edges: When enabled, Denoise attempts to sharpen the image at edges to prevent over-smoothing, though this can emphasize noise in some cases.
description.text:
Denoise: Uses spatial or temporal filtering to remove noise or grain without losing image quality.

Motion Input: An optional input for attaching pre-calculated motion vectors, such as those created by VectorGenerator. Denoise can generate motion vectors internally, but connecting this input may produce significantly faster results.

Temporal Processing: When enabled, uses frames on both sides of the current frame to perform temporal frame blending, which may produce a better denoise result. The number of frames used on either side of the current frame is determined by the Temporal Frame Offset control. When disabled, uses only the current frame to produce the denoise result.

Frame Blending: Sets the variance allowed between regions in blended frames. Higher values attempt to blend more regions, but can lose image detail. This control is only available when Temporal Processing is enabled.

Temporal Frame Offset: Sets the number of frames, on either side of the current frame, used to calculate the denoise effect.This control is only available when Temporal Processing is enabled.

Lift Blacks: When enabled, blacks in the image are lifted toward white. This can be particularly useful if your image contains a lot of sub-blacks, areas of black with a value less than 0.

Preserve Edges: When enabled, Denoise attempts to sharpen the image at edges to prevent over-smoothing, though this can emphasize noise in some cases.
